items.name: Night Blossom
items.description: A layered frozen drink of apple and limeade slushes topped with limeade foam and passion fruit boba, served non-alcoholic from the walk-up window in Pandora.
items.verdict: The rare novelty drink that is actually refreshing rather than just brightly colored. Ask for it without the foam if you want to taste the fruit layers properly.

items.name: Pineapple Cream Cheese Lumpia
items.description: A fried spring roll filled with pineapple and cream cheese, served hot in a paper sleeve alongside Pandora's specialty drinks.
items.verdict: Greasy, hot and better than it needs to be. Two of these and a Night Blossom is a legitimate cheap lunch if you do not mind eating standing up.

items.name: Beer with Blue Foam Topping
items.description: A pale ale served with a bright blue-green tropical foam floated on top, sold at the Pongu Pongu window as Pandora's alcoholic signature.
items.verdict: Overrated. It photographs beautifully and drinks like a decent beer with sweet foam ruining the head. Order the Night Blossom instead and get an actual beer at Dawa Bar.

items.name: Chargrilled Beef Bowl
items.description: Sliced chargrilled beef over your choice of base - quinoa and vegetable salad, rice and beans, or noodles - finished with a chimichurri-style sauce.
items.verdict: The best quick-service plate at Walt Disney World. Take the quinoa and vegetable base; it is the acid and crunch that makes the whole bowl work, and the rice base is a noticeably duller dish.

items.name: Cheeseburger Steamed Pods
items.description: Seasoned beef and cheese sealed inside soft steamed bao-style buns, served with a side of crunchy vegetable slaw or fries.
items.verdict: Order them as a shared starter, not a meal. Two adults splitting the pods and one bowl eat better and cheaper than two people each ordering their own entree.

items.name: Chili-Spiced Fried Tofu Bowl
items.description: Crisp chili-spiced fried tofu served over the same choice of bases and sauces as the meat bowls, built as its own dish rather than as a substitution.
items.verdict: The best vegan meal in any Walt Disney World park. It is not a consolation plate - the tofu is properly crisp and seasoned, and nobody has to explain anything at the counter.

items.name: Blueberry Cream Cheese Mousse
items.description: A cube of blueberry and cream cheese mousse over cake with a passion fruit layer, served cold and cut into a neat geometric block.
items.verdict: On the menu since opening day and still the best dessert under seven dollars in the park. Tart enough to cut the heat, which almost nothing else here manages.

items.name: Zebra Domes
items.description: Small domes of Amarula liqueur mousse over sponge cake, coated in white chocolate with dark chocolate stripes. The signature dessert of Disney's Animal Kingdom Lodge, sold inside the park here.
items.verdict: Worth walking into Harambe for. They travel badly in heat, so eat them within about ten minutes or carry them in the air conditioning back to your resort.

items.name: Karubi Ribs
items.description: Marinated grilled ribs served with rice or a street-corn style side from one of the four specialized windows at Harambe Market.
items.verdict: The best thing at Harambe Market and a smaller portion than Flame Tree's barbecue for similar money. Better cooking, less food - decide which you care about.

items.name: Gyro Flatbread
items.description: Seasoned grilled meat wrapped in warm flatbread with tomato, onion and a yogurt-based sauce, from the grill window at Harambe Market.
items.verdict: Solid, portable and unremarkable - the thing to order if you want to eat while walking to a Lion King showtime. Nobody has ever crossed a park for it.

items.name: Grilled Sausage Plate
items.description: A coiled grilled sausage in the South African boerewors style, served with a side from the dedicated sausage window in the Harambe Market courtyard.
items.verdict: Genuinely well-spiced and the item most guests walk straight past on the way to the ribs. Worth ordering if two of you are splitting across windows.

items.name: Dole Whip
items.description: The pineapple soft serve served in a cup or as a float, dairy-free and available at Animal Kingdom only from this Harambe counter.
items.verdict: The same product sold at three other spots on property, but with a shorter line and shaded seating behind the counter that almost nobody uses.

items.name: Dole Whip with Rum
items.description: Pineapple soft serve with rum added, sold at the Tamu Tamu window in Harambe - the Walt Disney World park location that serves this combination.
items.verdict: Sweet, strong enough to notice, and exactly right at 3 PM in July. This is the reason to walk to Tamu Tamu rather than getting a Dole Whip at any other park.

items.name: The Dawa
items.description: Vodka, honey and lime muddled to order in the glass at the open-air bar on the edge of Harambe. The name means medicine in Swahili.
items.verdict: The best cheap cocktail in the park - tart rather than sweet, and made rather than poured from a batch. Wait the extra ninety seconds it takes.

items.name: Safari Amber Lager
items.description: An amber lager brewed for Animal Kingdom and poured across the park's bars, most reliably at Dawa Bar in Harambe.
items.verdict: A perfectly good amber that you cannot get outside the parks, which is most of the appeal. Better than the novelty beer in Pandora at a lower price.

items.name: Turkey Leg
items.description: The smoked turkey leg sold from carts across Walt Disney World, brined until it tastes closer to ham than turkey and weighing well over a pound.
items.verdict: Overrated, and everybody figures that out on bite four. It is a photograph you eat a third of and carry around greasy for twenty minutes. Split it or skip it.

items.name: Fresh Whole Fruit
items.description: Whole fresh fruit sold from the shaded stand near the Kilimanjaro Safaris exit, rotating with what is being sourced.
items.verdict: The best value inside the gates and nobody writes about it. Three dollars of fruit does more for a hot afternoon than an eight dollar pretzel ever will.

items.name: Breakfast Sandwich
items.description: An egg and cheese sandwich on a roll or croissant from the Harambe bakery window, with meat or vegetarian options depending on the day.
items.verdict: Ordinary breakfast food in exactly the right place. Mobile order it while you are still on the safari truck and it is waiting when you walk out.

items.name: Tusker House Breakfast
items.description: The fixed-price character breakfast at Tusker House in Harambe, with American breakfast staples alongside spiced stews, chutneys and African-inspired dishes, hosted by Donald Duck and friends.
items.verdict: The best character meal at Walt Disney World for food quality, though lunch and dinner at the same restaurant are more interesting for barely more money. Book it only if being in the park early matters to you.

items.name: Ribs and Chicken Combo
items.description: Half a smoked chicken and a portion of pork ribs with two sides, served on a tray from the barbecue windows on Discovery Island.
items.verdict: The best value meal in the park. It feeds two adults who are not starving, and the smoke on the ribs is real rather than a sauce trick. Carry it down to the lower waterfront pavilions.

items.name: Pulled Pork Sandwich
items.description: Smoked pulled pork piled on a bun with a side, from the Discovery Island barbecue counters.
items.verdict: A properly good barbecue sandwich for under fifteen dollars, which at Walt Disney World is close to a miracle. The combo platter is better value if two of you are eating.

items.name: Baked Macaroni and Cheese with Pulled Pork
items.description: A bowl of baked macaroni and cheese topped with smoked pulled pork, sold from a small stand on Discovery Island with a menu of about three things.
items.verdict: Genuinely good mac and cheese from a cart, which is not a sentence you get to write often. Split it and take it to Flame Tree's waterfront pavilions.

items.name: Bread Service
items.description: A plate of warm breads with a set of house-made spreads and dips, served on the covered veranda at Nomad Lounge.
items.verdict: Sounds like a throwaway and is the best-value plate in the building. Order it with a cocktail on the veranda and you have the nicest thirty minutes available in this park.

items.name: Whole-Fried Sustainable Fish
items.description: A whole fish fried and served head-on with sauces and garnishes, the signature dish at the park's fine-dining restaurant since it opened in 2016.
items.verdict: The most ambitious plate in the park and worth ordering once if you are eating at Tiffins at all. It arrives whole and head-on, which is the point - do not order it for someone who will be upset by that.
